title: Homotopy and graded quasi-isomorphism invariance of the shift-filtered Hom complex
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], with Hom groups in a common larger universe. All complexes below are integer-indexed cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration, def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients] having a finite filtration interval independent of cochain degree. A filtered chain map and a filtered chain homotopy preserve every filtration step. Let $P,P'$ be bounded complexes and $I,J$ bounded-below complexes. Define the complex of abelian groups
$$C(P,I)^n=\bigoplus_i\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal A}(P^i,I^{i+n}),\qquad d(f)=d_If-(-1)^nf d_P,$$
with shift filtration
$$F^rC(P,I)^n=\{f\mid f^i(F^aP^i)\subseteq F^{a+r}I^{i+n}\text{ for every }a,i\}.$$
This is a bounded-below complex with a uniformly finite filtration. Precomposition by a filtered chain map $s:P'\to P$ and postcomposition by a filtered chain map $u:I\to J$ give filtered chain maps $s^*:C(P,I)\to C(P',I)$ and $u_*:C(P,I)\to C(P,J)$, commuting with one another and respecting identities and composition. Filtered-homotopic maps $s,t$ induce filtered-homotopic maps $s^*,t^*$, and filtered-homotopic maps $u,v$ induce filtered-homotopic maps $u_*,v_*$. In particular a filtered homotopy equivalence in either variable induces a filtered homotopy equivalence of these Hom complexes.

Suppose each $\operatorname{gr}^aI^n$ is injective in the extension-property sense [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. If $s:P'\to P$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism, meaning that every $\operatorname{gr}^as$ is an ordinary quasi-isomorphism, then $s^*:C(P,I)\to C(P',I)$ is a graded quasi-isomorphism. These assertions concern the concrete Hom complexes and their maps before localization.

The signed homotopy calculation and shift-filtration refinement are written out in report.md.
